papers.title: Advanced concentrative absorption meditation reorganizes functional connectivity gradients of the brain: 7T MRI and phenomenology case study of jhana meditation.
papers.abstract: There is growing scientific interest in advanced meditation, and particularly the Theravada Buddhist advanced concentrative absorption meditation known as jhana (ACAM-J). ACAM-J includes a series of eight consecutive meditative states, which are radically altered states of consciousness. The neuroscience of ACAM-J, specifically brain reorganization, remains underspecified in part due to the difficulty of finding and studying expert ACAM-J meditators and challenges related to laboratory investigation of ACAM-J. Using a nonlinear dimensionality reduction technique applied to human functional neuroimaging in an intensive case study, we investigated brain reorganization during ACAM-J. We applied linear mixed models and correlations to explore relations among brain reorganization and ACAM-J phenomenology. Results demonstrated that ACAM-J induces disruption of the hierarchical organization of the brain by shifting the gradients toward a more globally integrated rather than segregated state between sensory-related and higher-order cognitive regions. Additionally, ACAM-J induces a separation between sensory-related and attention modulation-related regions, resulting in greater differentiation in functional organization of these regions, consistent with phenomenological reports. This study highlights the need for further research into brain reorganization and health-related implications of both short-term and long-term practice of ACAM-J. Key points/highlights The neuroscience of advanced concentrative absorption meditation (ACAM) has the potential to improve our knowledge of well-being and altered states of consciousness but remains underexplored due to methodological challenges. We investigated functional reorganization of the brain during ACAM-J using gradient analysis and demonstrated that ACAM-J disrupts the hierarchical organization of the brain during meditation. Additionally, we demonstrated that ACAM-J increases differentiation between primary sensory areas and areas related to attention modulation.

papers.title: The neuroscience of highly stable, positive, and refined states of consciousness during jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J)
papers.abstract: Humans can experience a rich array of conscious experience, including highly stable, positive, and refined states of non-ordinary perception that can be elicited through advanced meditation. Here, we present the first group-level, ultra–high-field (7T) fMRI study of jhana advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J). We combined local (regional homogeneity), mesoscale (connectivity gradients), and global (geometric eigenmodes) human brain mapping with diverse and detailed phenomenology, meditative traits, behaviorally assessed cognitive functions, and extensive publicly available psychobehavioral affinity maps. Across eight successive states of ACAM-J, we observed reproducible neural trajectories marked by anterior-to-posterior reorganization, flattening of cortical hierarchies, nonlinear reconfiguration of global harmonics, and tight coupling between brain metrics and equanimity, attentional stability, and behavior. Neurosynth decoding further associate ACAM-J with reduced suffering-related processes and more with attentional monitoring. These findings suggest ACAM-J is a distinct, structured mode of awareness that persists despite radically reduced narrative thought and sensory content. Our findings also inform boundary conditions for current models of consciousness. More broadly, this research indicates that advanced meditation is a powerful framework for understanding psychological transformation, and for potential new opportunities for supporting human well-being and flourishing.

papers.title: Whole-Brain Models of Advanced Concentrative Absorption Meditation: Approaching Critical Dynamics through Jhāna
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation offers a powerful lens for investigating consciousness and for understanding how sustained training may contribute to human flourishing. In the spirit of neurophenomenology, we combine first-person reports with model-free empirical analyses and formal whole-brain modeling to investigate the mechanisms underlying advanced meditative states and minimal phenomenal experience (MPE). Specifically, we focus on jhāna meditation, a type of advanced concentrative absorption meditation (ACAM-J). Advanced practitioners accessed the eight ACAM-J states during ultra-high-field 7T functional magnetic resonance imaging. For each state, we first characterize empirical functional connectivity and then build a mechanistic whole-brain model that reproduces brain activity by modeling the dynamical regimes of different brain networks. We found that the later ACAM-J states, taken here as candidates for MPE, show increased large-scale functional integration and a shift of functional network dynamics toward near-critical working points. The default mode network (DMN) exhibits the largest shift, from a distant noise-driven regime during the control condition to near-critical dynamics during ACAM-J. We also observed that the trajectory of ACAM-J states is non-linear, with prominent reconfigurations at key meditative milestones. Our results suggest that MPE, as instantiated in later ACAM-J states, corresponds to a globally susceptible state where near-critical dynamics dominate. We interpret this near-critical regime as a form of “openness”, in which constrained and differentiated patterns of brain activity give way to greater flexibility. In particular, increased DMN susceptibility is correlated with broader attention and reduced narrative thought, consistent with a more 8lexible mode of self-related processing. In this context, advanced meditation provides a powerful model for studying how sustained contemplative practice can profoundly shape brain dynamics and provide a window into core aspects of consciousness.

papers.title: Electroencephalogram recordings in Jhana states: An open dataset
papers.abstract: The use of meditation as a tool to improve human wellbeing is receiving considerable scientific interest. However, most existing research has focused on concentration-based practices. One powerful alternative is jhana meditation, which leads to states characterised by self-reinforcing bliss, potentially useful for a variety of clinical and scientific domains. However, our understanding of these states is limited by small amounts of data and poor access to experts. To enable new insights, here we release the largest to date and first open-access dataset of electroencephalographic and physiological recordings in expert Jhana meditators. This includes 100+ hours of data in N=26 subjects across three retreats, alongside a detailed description and example code illustrating analysis of the data. This open dataset release can enable wider collaboration and has the potential to move us closer to an understanding of endogenously generated altered states of consciousness.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Jhana Advanced Concentrative Absorption Meditation Using 7 Tesla Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging
papers.abstract: Introduction: Jhana advanced concentrative absorption meditation (ACAM-J) involves profound changes in consciousness, making its neural correlates important for understanding consciousness and well-being. Prior neuroimaging has relied on univariate, group-level contrasts, leaving open whether ACAM-J carries distributed neural signatures decodable from individual scans. This study evaluates whether fMRI-derived regional homogeneity (ReHo) can classify ACAM-J using machine learning. Methods: We analysed 7T fMRI data from 20 advanced meditators who progressed through their standard ACAM-J sequence and two matched control tasks, plus intensive data from one case-study participant held out for final evaluation. ReHo maps were computed per segment and parcellated into 498 regions spanning cortex, subcortex, brainstem, and cerebellum. Within subject-wise stratified cross-validation, feature ranking, recursive feature elimination, and class balancing were applied to training data only; six classifier families were fitted, and the top three per contrast were combined by probability averaging. Results: Across 19 binary comparisons, the ensemble reached an overall average accuracy of 65.87% before and 66.82% after regressing out phenomenology-related variance, with an average Cohen's \k{appa} of 0.2443. Discrimination was strongest for the most separated states (ACAM-J1 vs ACAM-J6, 74.33% accuracy, \k{appa} = 0.5158), while adjacent states were harder to separate. Prefrontal and anterior cingulate areas contributed most to model decisions. Conclusion: ReHo patterns measured at 7T carry information distinguishing ACAM-J from control states and, more modestly, from one another, supporting the feasibility of multivariate decoding of advanced meditation and informing future work on its mechanisms and neuromodulation.

papers.title: Meditative absorption shifts brain dynamics toward criticality
papers.abstract: Criticality describes a regime between order and chaos that supports flexible yet stable information processing. Here we examine whether neural dynamics can be volitionally shifted toward criticality through the self-regulation of attention. We examined ten experienced practitioners of meditation during a 10-day retreat, comparing refined states of meditative absorption, called the jhanas, to regular mindfulness of breathing. We collected electroencephalography (EEG) and physiological data during these practices and quantified the signal's dynamical properties using Lempel-Ziv complexity, signal entropy, chaoticity and long-range temporal correlations. In addition, we estimated perturbational sensitivity using a global auditory oddball mismatch negativity (MMN) during meditation. Relative to mindfulness, jhana was associated with pronounced self-reported sensory fading, slower respiration, higher neural signal diversity across multiple measures, reduced chaoticity, and enhanced MMN amplitude over frontocentral sites. Spectral analyses showed a flatter aperiodic one over f component and a frequency-specific reorganization of long-range temporal correlations. Together, increased diversity with reduced chaoticity and heightened deviance detection indicate a shift toward a metastable, near-critical regime during jhana. We propose an overlap of the phenomenology of jhana with minimal phenomenal experiences in terms of progressive attenuation of sensory content with preserved tonic alertness. Accordingly, our findings suggest that criticality is a candidate neurophysiological marker of the absorptive, minimal-content dimension of the minimal phenomenal experience.

papers.title: Samatha Bhāvanā: Studi Komprehensif Teknik Pengembangan Ketenangan, Hambatan, dan Pencapaian Batin
papers.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji secara komprehensif praktik Samatha Bhāvanā sebagai metode pengembangan ketenangan batin dalam tradisi Buddhis Theravāda, dengan fokus pada teknik pelaksanaan, hambatan, serta pencapaian batin yang dihasilkan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kepustakaan terhadap teks-teks klasik seperti Visuddhimagga dan Tipiṭaka (edisi PTS), serta didukung oleh kajian ilmiah kontemporer dalam bidang psikologi dan neuroscience. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Samatha Bhāvanā merupakan praktik meditasi yang sistematis dan bertahap, dimulai dari pemilihan objek meditasi berdasarkan carita (karakter mental), pengembangan konsentrasi melalui kemunculan nimitta, hingga pencapaian jhāna sebagai puncak konsentrasi. Selain itu, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi adanya hambatan utama dalam praktik meditasi yang terbagi menjadi nīvaraṇa (hambatan internal) dan palibodha (hambatan eksternal), yang secara signifikan mempengaruhi kualitas konsentrasi. Keberhasilan praktik sangat ditentukan oleh kemampuan praktisi dalam mengelola hambatan tersebut secara simultan. Lebih lanjut, pencapaian lanjutan dalam Samatha Bhāvanā mencakup penguasaan meditasi (vasī) dan perkembangan kesadaran tingkat tinggi (abhiññā), yang menunjukkan optimalisasi fungsi mental dan stabilitas batin. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa Samatha Bhāvanā tidak hanya memiliki landasan filosofis yang kuat, tetapi juga relevan dengan temuan ilmiah modern terkait peningkatan perhatian, regulasi emosi, dan kesejahteraan psikologis. Dengan demikian, praktik ini memiliki potensi besar untuk diintegrasikan dalam konteks pendidikan dan kesehatan mental.

papers.title: Peace and the Unconditioned: Nibbāna as the Supreme Pacification
papers.abstract:
Abstract
This article argues that early Buddhist discourse in the Sutta Piṭaka construes peace not as mere emotional calm or social quietism but as the pacification (upasama) that culminates in nibbāna, the unconditioned. Reading key formulae “nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ,” “stilling of all formations” (sabbasaṅkhārasamatho), and epithets such as santi (peace) and khema (security) the study clarifies how “supreme happiness” denotes qualitative freedom from affliction rather than hedonic pleasure. It maps the semantic field of peace within the soteriological sequence nibbidā virāga nirodha upasama/vimutti, and shows how the path functions as a technology of pacification: ethical discipline (sīla) removes remorse and fear, concentration (samādhi/jhāna) stills the hindrances and unifies attention, and insight (vipassanā) discloses anicca–dukkha anattā, deconstructing craving and clinging. The article addresses common misreadings (nihilism, quietism) and proposes that the Nikāyas present peace as the non-arising of stress grounded in dependent origination’s cessation, with practical implications for contemplative training and communal concord.

papers.title: Technical Evaluation of the Smart Water Jug-Plastic Bottle Disposal System
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the technical performance and behavioral impact of the Smart Water Jug–Plastic Bottle Disposal System (SWJ – PBDS) as a strategy at Ocampo National High School – Senior High School (ONHS-SHS). The research addressed the escalating issue of plastic waste, focusing on reducing plastic bottle consumption through innovative smart sensor technology. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining descriptive and quasi-experimental designs. The descriptive component details the system’s characteristics via surveys, gathering data on user experiences and operational aspects. The quasi-experimental component assesses the system’s impact on waste management outcomes using a pre-test and post-test survey to compare waste reduction before and after the implementation of the research product.
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

papers.title: Professionalism and Growth Pathways of Education Graduates: The Contribution of Work Experience
papers.abstract: The professionalism and career growth pathways of education graduates from Indiana Aerospace University and private schools in Lapu-Lapu City between 2021 and 2025. Anchored in Kolb’s Experiential Learning, Bandura’s Social Learning, and Super’s Career Development theories, it explores how practical work experience enhances graduates’ teaching competencies, professional ethics, and career development. The research employed a quantitative descriptive design with 100 respondents comprising education graduates from Indiana Aerospace University and private schools in Lapu-Lapu City, selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected via structured questionnaires distributed through Google Forms, focusing on respondents’ profiles, work experience, professionalism, growth, and encountered challenges. Findings show that education graduates strongly agree on the vital role of work experience in developing practical skills, professional conduct, confidence, and continuous learning opportunities. Graduates report that hands-on experience positively influences their problem-solving abilities, adaptability, and clarity in career goals. However, significant challenges include poor professionalism among colleagues, inconsistent professional behavior, lack of support for growth, and limited career advancement opportunities, which adversely impact the work environment and motivation. The study concludes that work experience is pivotal in fostering professionalism and career growth in education graduates, reinforcing practical training and ongoing professional development. Recommendations include implementing clear professional standards, enhancing support for growth initiatives, and establishing career advancement pathways to address identified problems. The proposed action plan aims to promote a positive work environment, ethical conduct, and sustained professional development, ultimately improving educational outcomes and graduate employability.
papers.journal: Journal of Advanced Studies in Aviation, Aerospace, and Management

papers.title: Investigating the complex cortical dynamics of an advanced concentrative absorption meditation called jhanas (ACAM-J): a geometric eigenmode analysis.
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation has been associated with long- and short-term psychological changes such as bliss, profound insight, and transformation of well-being. However, most advanced meditation neuroimaging analyses have implemented primarily spatially-localized approaches, focusing on discrete regional changes in activity rather than distributed dynamics. The present study uses a geometric eigenmode decomposition of ultrahigh field-strength 7T functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from an intensely sampled case study to investigate the complex, distributed cortical dynamics associated with advanced concentrative absorption meditation. Geometric eigenmode decomposition of advanced concentrative absorption meditation and non-meditative control task fMRI data revealed elevated global brain state power and energy patterns of specific advanced concentrative absorption meditation states compared to controls, with mid-frequency spectrum brain state power and energy following a non-random, cubic trajectory through the advanced concentrative absorption meditation sequence. Further, these brain state differences were meaningfully associated with subjective phenomenological reports of attention, intensity of advanced concentrative absorption meditation quality, and sensations. This study unites precise methodological design, a novel fMRI decomposition framework, and rigorous phenomenology to provide valuable insights into the distributed neural signatures of highly refined conscious states. These results underscore similarities and differences between advanced concentrative absorption meditation and other altered states of consciousness like those induced by psychedelics-offering insights into refined conscious states and their implications for health and well-being.

papers.title: An Ethical Samādhi: Brahma-vihāra Meditation and the Flexible Early Buddhist Path
papers.abstract: This article offers a new interpretation of Brahma-vihāra meditation (BVM) in early Buddhism, positioning it between ethical cultivation and development of samādhi; BVM can thereby perfect ethical practice by creating a comprehensive meditative state that is thoroughly ethical. The fact that the radically ethical states of mind of BVM are sometimes included in the path to liberation, while more commonly they are not, further affords an important understanding regarding the flexible nature of the early Buddhist path. This is not one path, two paths, or any other number of paths, but a flexible method that different practitioners can use in various ways, evoking its diverse potentials according to their personal inclinations and contexts. Within this dynamic structure, Brahma-vihāra meditations play two main roles: first, they allow a completion of ethical practice, bringing it to perfection through the divine attitudes of love (mettā), compassion (karuṇā), empathic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekkhā). Second, these states of mind, in which the mind reaches a state of totality, serve as a form of samādhi, which can replace other types of meditative concentration, such as jhāna. At their best, these states can be liberating. This interpretation of BVM’s role improves our understanding of the early Buddhist path, and specifically of the manner in which it combines ethical cultivation with advanced meditation. Here, samādhi proves to be ethical, and ethics liberating.

papers.title: An mHealth Stress Management Intervention for Latino Millennial Caregivers: Pilot Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Latino millennial caregivers comprise over one-quarter of millennial family caregivers in the United States. Latino millennial family caregivers face unique challenges due to cultural, structural, and economic burdens that may increase stress and stress-related health effects. These caregivers also report time limitations due to their multiple roles. Technology may be a way to deliver an accessible and flexible intervention to support stress management and emotional regulation in this population. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a culturally tailored mobile health (mHealth) intervention to support stress management and emotional regulation for Latino millennial caregivers. METHODS: Participants (N=30) were recruited nationally in the United States using a recruitment agency and were randomized to the intervention or waitlist control groups. The 4-week fully automated intervention included daily mindfulness exercises and journaling prompts delivered via a custom mHealth platform. The waitlist control group received a written handout with mindfulness, journaling, and support information. Feasibility data, including recruitment and retention rates and intervention adherence, and postintervention acceptability surveys were collected. Study outcome measures were collected electronically at baseline and 2, 4, and 6 weeks. Primary outcomes included caregiver burden and perceived stress, and secondary outcomes included well-being, informational support, and emotional support. Feasibility and acceptability data were analyzed descriptively alongside study outcome measure data from participants who completed week 6 data collection (n=21). No efficacy testing was conducted. RESULTS: Enrollment was completed in 12 weeks (N=30), with a 70% (21/30) retention. Participants showed differential adherence, with 60% (6/10) completing a daily journal activity and 30% (3/10) completing a daily mindfulness activity. Adherence patterns were reflected in the acceptability findings, with journaling being preferred over mindfulness. Preliminary outcomes showed varying patterns between the intervention and control groups, with the intervention group showing decreased median burden levels from before (median 20, IQR 15-27.25) to after the intervention (median 15, IQR 10.50-28.75) but increased median stress levels from 19.50 (IQR 12-26.75) to 21 (IQR 8.75-22.75), while the control group burden and stress levels remained the same before and after the intervention. Positive affect and well-being and informational support increased for both groups. Median emotional support levels increased from 15 (IQR 12-20) before the intervention to 16 (IQR 13-19) after the intervention for the control group and decreased from 14.5 (IQR 11.5-17.75) to 14 (IQR 12-17.25) for the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: Findings demonstrate areas for further intervention iteration to address both adherence and acceptability issues with the mindfulness component of the intervention. Intervention implementation also needs to be addressed, including participant retention rates. Our team will use lessons learned alongside feedback from Latino millennial caregivers to address these issues.

papers.title: Brief Motivational Workplace Intervention to Reduce Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Consumption Among Health Care Workers: Intervention Description, Feasibility, Fidelity, and Exploratory Outcomes From a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic disease, including type 2 diabetes, is a major public health concern. Reducing sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption is a critical target for disease prevention and lifestyle modification. Workplace interventions offer a promising opportunity to address barriers to behavior change while strengthening motivation and self-efficacy. OBJECTIVE: The authors describe the intervention protocol, fidelity, and feasibility of a theory-informed brief intervention based on motivational interviewing principles to support reductions in SSB consumption among health care workers. The authors also explore changes over time in proposed mechanisms of behavior change. METHODS: Participants (N=314) allocated to the intervention arm of a multicenter randomized controlled trial received a 4-dose intervention consisting of an introductory phone call, a brief counseling session, and 2 booster calls, supplemented by at-home tools targeting stress and craving management. We assessed fidelity to motivational interviewing principles (competence scores) and described feasibility via session adherence. Finally, we explored changes over time in motivation for change and perceived self-efficacy. RESULTS: More than 60% of enrolled participants completed all 4 sessions, suggesting feasibility and high retention in the context of a remotely delivered workplace intervention. Health coaches achieved basic levels of proficiency in 2 of 4 competency scores: technical (mean 3.23, SD 0.48) and complex reflections (mean 41.91%, SD 15.17%). Preliminary exploratory findings indicate improvements in motivation for change and self-efficacy over time. Finally, we found that the use of brief mindfulness practices were associated with acute reductions in stress and cravings. CONCLUSIONS: This theory-grounded brief motivational intervention may offer a cost-effective and accessible approach for employers to support behavior change related to SSB consumption. Findings from the fully powered randomized controlled trial are needed to determine if the brief intervention can effectively change behavior. This paper establishes the intervention and its framework to inform future implementation.

papers.title: Mindfulness-based orofacial pain education promotes perceived control and self-management in painful TMD.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The added value of mindfulness-based strategies for chronic painful temporomandibular disorders (TMD) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate an 8-week Mindfulness-Based Orofacial Pain Education Program added to conventional care. METHODS: This mixed-methods quasi-experimental controlled study included 53 adults receiving conventional care plus the program ( RESULTS: No group-by-time interaction was found for the primary outcome (WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain; β = 0.165; 95% CI, -0.113-0.442;  CONCLUSIONS: The program did not improve most clinical outcomes but fostered perceived pain control and engagement in self-management beyond symptom reduction.
papers.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice

papers.title: When night owls confront work deadlines: a dual‑system perspective on how and when chronotype relates to procrastination.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study examines the association between chronotype and procrastination. Drawing on the hot-cool distinction between the emotional and cognitive systems of self-control, we propose that negative mood and future temporal perspective mediate this association as hot- and cool-system pathways, respectively, with dispositional mindfulness moderating these indirect effects. METHODS: Study 1 ( RESULTS: In Study 1, a later chronotype significantly predicted subsequent procrastination, whereas the reverse cross-lagged paths were not significant. Study 2 indicated that negative mood and future temporal perspective mediated the positive association between later chronotype and procrastination and that dispositional mindfulness significantly attenuated the mediating effect of negative mood but did not moderate the mediation  CONCLUSIONS: These findings offer longitudinal evidence linking chronotype to procrastination. Individuals with a later chronotype appear more prone to procrastination, possibly owing to elevated negative mood and a diminished future temporal perspective. Notably, dispositional mindfulness appears to mitigate the indirect relationship between later chronotype and procrastination

papers.title: Effect of yoga on blood pressure in hypertensive older adults: a randomised multicentre study with control group - study protocol.

authors.name: João Batista Costa Carvalho De Serro-Azul

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is highly prevalent among older adults and remains a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Age-related arterial stiffness and endothelial dysfunction contribute to residual cardiovascular risk despite adequate brachial blood pressure control. Yoga is a mind–body intervention integrating physical postures, breathing techniques and meditation that has demonstrated modest blood pressure-lowering effects in adults; however, evidence in older hypertensive populations remains limited. METHODS: This prospective, randomised, controlled, multicentre study will include ninety (n=90) community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older with treated hypertension, randomised in a 2:1 ratio to a 12-week structured, senior-adapted yoga programme plus usual care (n=60) or to usual care with attention-control health education sessions (n=30). The primary outcome is the between-group difference in change in brachial systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks. Secondary exploratory outcomes include ambulatory and central blood pressure, arterial stiffness, endothelial function, functional capacity, sleep parameters, quality of life, mood status and feasibility metrics. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: All participants will provide written informed consent prior to enrolment. The study has been approved by the Comitê de Ética em Pesquisa do Hospital das Clínicas, Faculdade de Medicina, Universidade de São Paulo (CEP HC-FMUSP; approval number 8.068.380). The study will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki (World Medical Association, 2013). It was registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC) on 19 February 2026 as ‘Yoga in Elderly Hypertensive Patients’, identifier RBR-23vmpsx (https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-23vmpsx). Recruitment began in June 2026 and is expected to be completed by April 2027. Funding is provided by the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo (FAPESP; process 2024/23879-2). The sponsor, Instituto do Coração (InCor), will oversee study monitoring, with annual audits planned.

papers.title: WE PLAY | ON JOUE - Family-Centered Virtual Reality Games Room for Children with Developmental Disabilities and Their Families: A Feasibility Case Study.
papers.abstract: AIMS: To explore the feasibility, satisfaction with, enjoyment of, acceptability, and preliminary effects of joint virtual reality (VR) sessions targeting physical engagement in youth with disabilities and relaxation in caregivers. METHODS: In a mini-ethnographic case study, four youth-caregiver dyads completed weekly 30-minute immersive VR sessions over four weeks. Youth (aged 10-20 years) with cerebral palsy ( RESULTS: Although standardized motor outcomes showed limited overall change over the intervention period, improvements were observed in one youth participant. Reductions in stress were noted for three caregivers. Enjoyment ratings were high (7-10/10 for youth; 9-10/10 for caregivers), with engaging gameplay and relaxation identified as key benefits. CONCLUSIONS: Findings provide preliminary support for the potential feasibility and acceptability of family-centered VR interventions in pediatric rehabilitation, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

papers.title: The relation between mindfulness and mentalizing among individuals with borderline personality disorder: A controlled study.
papers.abstract: Mentalizing-the capacity to consider mental states-is a core human ability, yet processes related to it remain poorly understood. Mindfulness has been proposed as functionally related to mentalizing, but the nature and direction of this relation remain unclear. Although both are relevant to borderline personality disorder (BPD), research has rarely examined them together. This study examined group differences in and associations between dispositional mindfulness and mentalizing among individuals with BPD, psychiatric controls (PCs), and healthy controls (HCs). Participants were 153 adults (51 per group) completing diagnostic and laboratory assessments. Mindfulness was measured with the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire, and mentalizing with the Mentalization Scale and Reflective Functioning Scale applied to the Brief Reflective Function Interview. papers.title: "My Body is Nurturing Me" Personalized Spiritual Experiences during Interoceptive Awareness Training Among People in Medication Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder.
papers.abstract: Research links the neural processes of spiritual experiences, or 'peak experiences' of eudaimonic well-being, to substance abuse recovery. Studies also identify health improvements among substance use disorder (SUD) treatment approaches that include interoceptive awareness training. However, the relationship between interoceptive awareness and spiritual experience within substance use recovery is poorly understood. This conceptual project was designed to explore personalized spiritual experience among a sub-set of participants in a study of Mindful Awareness in Body-oriented Therapy (MABT) for people in medication treatment for opioid use disorder (MOUD). MABT teaches and develops the capacity for interoceptive awareness, defined as the conscious experience of internal bodily sensations, to facilitate improved self-care and well-being. Three themes of spiritual experience emerged based on consistent patterns and processes: Experiencing Wholeness and Healing, Awakening Inner Knowing, and My Body is Nurturing Me. To illustrate how these themes are expressed within the context of MABT, four participant exemplars are provided. Responses to survey questions about spiritual experience and interoceptive awareness were also examined. All participants endorsed some level of SE and the level of IA increased pre to post. In summary, this project highlighted the role of SE in MABT and the potential helpfulness of SE in SUD recovery. Future research could explore underlying mechanisms of IA for improved SE and the role of SE in SUD recovery.
